mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant increase following a FEDFUNDS decrease of more than 0.25% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the last month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant decrease following a UNRATE increase of more than 0.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant increase following a sustained rise in HOUST (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant decrease following a decrease in INDPRO of more than 1% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant increase following a PAYEMS increase of more than 200,000 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in the last month, it signals increased consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant increase following a RSAFS increase of more than 1% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant decrease when FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% in the last quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% in 3 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not show a statistically significant increase when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% (p > 0.05).
